answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed walnut grove where every tree carries a uniquely carved cipher tag. The steward tends the grove a full season, and random spot-checks summon the holder to read one tag aloud on camera beside that exact tree, velvet gloves proving hands-on care. One steward cannot tend two groves at once, and the grove lease fee in outside money doubles per further grove on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real grove, another season of labor, another human, and twice the prior fee.
